My ride or die🫶🏻🫶🏻🫶🏻. Sinceramente, lo que comenzó por una casualidad en la App Store, se convirtió en una de las apps que más uso día a día. Al iniciar la App, solicita tomar fotos de tu rostro para identificar las características y problemas que presente y te da una puntuación del 1-100, en base a 5 categorías (y este proceso se repite 1 vez cada semana para ver el progreso de acuerdo a tu nuevo rutina) te hace una serie de preguntas para descubrir cuál es la causa de los problemas en tu piel, si tienes comedones, espinillas, acné fungico, etc. 

Después te pide que si quieres puedes ingresar los productos en tu rutina para ver si son aptos para tu tipo de piel ( y si no es el caso, te da alternativas más aptas😮‍💨😮‍💨). Viene integrada con IA para un mejor asesoramiento ya sea de tu rutina, productos, hasta para encontrar dupes🥹🥹🥹.

En mi caso, mi limpiador, según mi tipo de piel, no era para uso diario porque tenía ácido salicílico y me había comprado el suero de ácido azelaico de Anua, entonces me recomendó la primera semana introducirlo en mi rutina 2 veces por la noche (porque mi piel es sensible) y si mi piel lo toleraba, que aumentara a 3-4 veces pero por la noche y me ha ido muy bien en estas dos semanas que llevo usándola.

Espero que te haya servido mi reseña y que decidas instalarte la app😌🪄.

App has a lot of potential. Used the 3 day free trail and made sure I explored and tried every feature. At the beginning it interviews you on your skin type and skin goals, you’re able to choose multiple (three in total) some examples being Redness,Enlarged pores and Oiliness. From there it asks for pictures of your face from different angles in good lighting and a list products you use in the skincare routine you can search yourself or take pictures of your products and they find it for you. Unfortunately they couldn’t find my correct cleanser ether way, just the same brand. They did find everything else in my routine correctly though and classify them accordingly. I do have a toner that also acts as a chemical exfoliant that they put under exfoliants, leaving the toner sublist blank. 

From this it gives you two scores out of 100, one for how “good” your skin looks and one for how good your skin routine is for your goals. It does give a disclaimer that how “good” your skin is is subjective which I appreciate. It’ll tell you whether the product is a good match because of certain ingredients that help your goals. 

If you have a cleanser, moisturizer and sunscreen your score is 80. It suggests to add a toner and serum to improve score but adding doesn’t get you to 100. It doesn’t show how to improve your score from there or which cleansers, moisturizers or other products would be better than what you already have. It does give you suggestions per category, adding all the options however doesn’t give you a score of 100, 89 at most (for me at least). 

You can update your photos of your face and it does increase your score. There’s five categories of criteria. Complexion, Acne and Texture, Barrier and Hydration, Fine lines and wrinkles and Eye bags dark circles. I’ve took 6 pictures “check ups” in the last 2 days and at least one of the categories increase every time (same lighting and pose). I don’t know if it’s accurate or if it’s just to give us hope that are skins getting better. 

This app does use A.I. specifically in its chat. You ask it a sentence like “ What are peptides” or “What products are best for me. It doesn’t continue a conversation, it gives you its answer no clarification if asked. If you ask for dupes on a product, asking for additional dupes doesn’t get you any other dupes just the same suggestions. It doesn’t find products that meet the exact qualifications in the prompt and some questions when hit enter don’t even go through. Asking to find med spa just leads you to the AI chat…this app is pretty heavily reliant on A.I for a lot of its features, just bringing you back to the chat bot for features like “Find med spa” and “Ask a derm”.

It shows if products are vegan free, silicone free, alcohol free, fungal acne face and all sorts of other stuff. I do wish it said if sunscreens had white casts though. 

It educates you on skincare treatment like micro needling ect. 

Under products it shows links to social media reviews, reviews under are usually all from Reddit and a lot of products it suggestions don’t have any social media reviews and aren’t that popular. 

It shows a wide variety of products from brands I didn’t even know existed which is kind of nice to know what’s all out there. 

Overall I would consider subscribing in the future because generally I really like this app aesthetic and what it’s trying to due but it needs some work. 

Suggestions:
-Say if a product leaves a whitecast
- Remove “Try product” till feature is available”
-Show the exact math and criteria for Skin Care Routine score
-Improve A.I and get rid of thinking orb looks to much like Siri.
-Add filters to categories such as “Devices” for example:what this helps with, cost ect. A big list isn’t helpful 
-Add TikTok social media reviews

I don’t usually write reviews, but Thea genuinely changed my relationship with my skin, so I felt I had to share. For the longest time, I struggled with oily, acne-prone, sensitive skin, and no matter what I tried, I felt stuck, frustrated, and honestly insecure. I was constantly breaking out, confused about products, and losing confidence.

Since using Thea, my skin has calmed down so much. My breakouts are less frequent, my texture is smoother, and my skin finally looks healthier and more balanced instead of constantly irritated. Even the redness I hated seeing in the mirror has improved. For the first time, I actually enjoy doing my skincare instead of fearing it it.

What really changed my life is the education this app gives. I finally understood what ingredients were helping me and what was secretly making my skin worse. I stopped over-exfoliating, stopped using the wrong products, and built a routine that actually works for me. The dupe finder and match scores helped me find affordable products without wasting money on things that didn’t suit my skin.

My favorite features are the personalized routines, ingredient explanations, and progress tracking. It feels like I have a real skincare expert guiding me every day. The app doesn’t just recommend it explains, and that made all the difference for me.

Because of Thea, my skin is healthier, but more importantly, my confidence is coming back. I feel more comfortable in my own skin again, and that feeling is priceless. If you’re struggling, confused, or tired of trial and error like I was this app is truly worth it. 💖

A great skincare resource!. I’ve been using Thea for a couple months now and it’s a game changer! Yes, you need to pay for the app in order to get the full benefits, but for the amount I’ve used it I’d say it’s worth it! I LOVE that it shows you if a product is a good match for you skin and highlights the ingredients, bonus is that it links reviews that are from real users (a lot of useful Reddit threads). Since using Thea I have a better understanding of my skins needs and my skin has been glowing.

My #1 Skincare App. Thea has actually made a huge difference in my routine and I’m so grateful for this app!

Since using it, I’ve had way fewer breakouts, especially stubborn closed comedones that I get on my cheeks sometimes. My skin also feels less irritated and reactive because I can quickly check ingredients and avoid anything with parfum/fragrance or other triggers that used to make my skin red.

I added all my skincare into the app, so whenever I’m repurchasing something, I just check Thea first. It keeps my routine more consistent and helps me avoid things that don’t agree with my sensitive skin. I’m definitely buying smarter now because I don’t buy more products with ingredients I (now) know will irritate me.

My favorite features are the ingredient checker and the match score. I really only use products with a great match now, and it’s made my routine feel a lot more tailored to my skin. I’ve even discovered some amazing K-beauty products through the app that I probably wouldn’t have tried otherwise.

Overall, I highly recommend Thea if you want personalized skincare routines (and even makeup help). I’m thinking about trying the monthly subscription just to test the paid features. If I do, I’ll update my thoughts!
